title: Villain vs. Villain: Philly Topples Brucie, and the Top of the Table Becomes a Four-Way Pileup
dek: Team Pillbert hands No Banner only HULK its first loss, Zoe and Kaushal pull off big upsets, and Alan spends the week running the busiest trade desk in the league.
body: The Buckaroo Football League finally got the matchup it was built for: the league's resident jerk against the guy everyone loves rooting against. Alan's Team Pillbert went into Week 4 with a 28 percent win chance against Ramon's undefeated No Banner only HULK and came out with a 125.42 to 116.72 win. That leaves the room with a real dilemma. Do you celebrate Brucie's first loss, or mourn Philly's third straight win? The correct answer is to do both, loudly, and preferably near Ramon's controller.

The villain's win had fingerprints all over the trade market. Javonte Williams, freshly acquired from Randy for Stefon Diggs, dropped 28.8 points on a 13.25 projection in his Pillbert debut. Yes, you read that right: Randy made a trade. The league's most tight-fisted manager finally opened the vault, and his old running back immediately went off for the guy in the black hat. Alan also left Kyle Monangai's 27.5 points on his bench and still won, which is exactly the kind of thing that makes a villain unbearable. Kenneth Walker III's 30.4 for the HULK was not enough to save Brucie's perfect record.

The other upset of the week belongs to Zoe, the rookie who is learning this league at an alarming speed. Ghostu-Spider SZN entered with a 29 percent chance against the defending champ and beat The Horse is Hea 120.88 to 95.1. Tetairoa McMillan put up the best game in the league at 38.2 points on a 13.5 projection, and Bijan Robinson added 27.2. Z Squared even left Nico Collins and his 27.3 points on the bench and still won by more than 25. Sonny, meanwhile, got 1.5 points from Parker Washington and watched Chuba Hubbard, whom he just traded Rashee Rice to Ramon to get, score 25.4 on his bench. The commissioner can rewrite the rules on the website, but he can't change his lineup after kickoff.

Over in Randy's matchup, The fumblers were 61 percent favorites and got flattened 140.1 to 96.88 by Kaushal's Habibsters, the highest score of the week. CeeDee Lamb went for 32.8 on a 13.65 projection, and Habib finally put a W on the board after an 0-3 start. Speeding past the law is nothing new for him, but speeding past a 3-0 team is a welcome change. And the cruelest stat in the league: Kaushal's 459.1 points for is fourth-best in the league, ahead of Randy's 458.7, and he's 1-3. The two-time champ has been the unluckiest man in the Buckaroo all season. Mekhi got his first win too, as Dawgs beat Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 107.54 to 90.22. Kyren Williams scored 31.7 on an 11.88 projection, which was plenty to cover for Ja'Marr Chase's 4.2-point dud.

The standings now feature a four-way tie at 3-1: No Banner only HULK, Team Pillbert, The Horse is Hea, and The fumblers. Ramon still leads the pack with 561 points for, a massive cushion, and 98 percent playoff odds, but his title odds slid from 54 to 43 percent. Alan's title odds more than doubled from 9 to 20 percent, while Sonny's got cut from 20 to 11 and Randy's dipped from 15 to 13. Zoe sits alone at 2-2 with 17 percent playoff odds. Kaushal (39 percent) and Mekhi (22 percent) are 1-3 and still very much breathing. JMoney is 0-4 with 349.2 points for and a playoff probability of zero, which a numbers guy will appreciate for its clean, round honesty.

The wire was busy too. Alan drafted his own sequel: he flipped Ashton Jeanty in from Jordan for Isaiah Likely, Emeka Egbuka and Denzel Boston, then sent Jeanty and Davante Adams to Mekhi for Justin Jefferson. He also dropped De'Von Achane, cut Bryce Young, and picked up Tyreek Hill, Kalif Raymond and Ollie Gordon II. Sonny scooped up Bryce Young, swapped J.K. Dobbins for Tony Pollard, dropped Mark Andrews, and grabbed the Bears D/ST, proof that even a Boston address can't wash Chicago out. Jordan added Kirk Cousins over Marvin Harrison Jr., and Kaushal swapped Drake Maye for Sam Darnold. Ramon picked up Jason Myers from Alan's discard pile and, of course, the Bills D/ST, because the turncoat must be fed. Randy signed Trevor Lawrence in place of Justin Herbert and added Darren Waller and Jordan Addison.

Week 5 is loaded. Mekhi hosts Alan in the revenge game nobody needed but everyone wants: Kai gets Jeanty and Adams against the guy who sent them over. Ramon and Randy meet in a 3-1 heavyweight bout, with Brucie trying to stop a slide and Randy trying to prove he's still a contender, trade or no trade. Kaushal gets Sonny in the battle of Bowl winners: Habibsters' three rings against the reigning champ. And JMoney hosts Zilgit in a matchup that could get awkward at home. Zoe is hot, Jordan is 0-4, and the numbers don't look kind.

social.author: Buckaroo Insider
social.text: Sources confirm Randy has made a trade. Repeat: Randy has made a trade. Javonte Williams immediately scored 28.8 for Alan. Sources also confirm Randy is complaining about it.

social.author: HULK Hate Watch
social.text: No Banner only HULK is no longer undefeated. Somewhere a controller just hit a wall. Thoughts and prayers to the drywall.

social.author: Team Pillbert Ultras
social.text: 28 percent win chance. Benched 27.5 points. Still won. You can boo us all you want, we can't hear you over the W3 streak.

social.author: Ghostu-Spider Nation
social.text: Tetairoa McMillan 38.2. Bijan 27.2. 27.3 sitting on the bench. Our rookie GM just beat the defending champ by 25 and she wasn't even trying that hard.

social.author: Commish Accountability Project
social.text: Sonny traded Rashee Rice for Chuba Hubbard and then benched Chuba for his 25.4-point game. The Boston air is getting to him.

social.author: Habib Hive
social.text: 140.1 points. Highest in the league. Fourth in points for. Record: 1-3. The two-time champ is not slumping, the schedule just has it out for him.

social.author: The Waiver Wire Report
social.text: Alan made two trades, dropped Achane, cut Bryce Young, and added three guys. Sonny picked up Bryce Young. Ramon picked up Alan's kicker. Philly is basically running a thrift store now.

social.author: Dawgs Den
social.text: Chase gives us 4.2 and we still win by 17 behind 31.7 from Kyren. Now Kai gets Jeanty and Adams against the guy who traded them. Circle Week 5.

social.author: Numbers Don't Lie Pod
social.text: Counting or not Counting GV is 0-4 with 0 percent playoff odds. JMoney, we've counted. It's not counting.

bios.1: The defending champ is 3-1 but just took a 25-point beating from a rookie while Chuba Hubbard's 25.4 sat on the bench. Sonny's title odds fell from 20 to 11 percent, and a date with two-time champ Kaushal awaits.
bios.2: Randy did the unthinkable and made a trade, then got crushed 140.1 to 96.88 as a 61 percent favorite. Still 3-1 with 13 percent title odds, but the shine is gone heading into a top-of-the-table clash with Ramon.
bios.3: JMoney is 0-4 with a league-low 349.2 points and a playoff probability of exactly zero. A busy week of moves brought in Kirk Cousins, Emeka Egbuka and more, but the math remains brutally clear.
bios.4: Alan has won three straight, toppled the HULK as a 28 percent underdog, and more than doubled his title odds to 20 percent. He also flipped half his roster in a week, so whatever this team looks like next Sunday, the bad guy is winning.
bios.5: Mekhi got off the schneid with a 107.54-point win, thanks to Kyren Williams' 31.7. Now armed with Jeanty and Adams from the Alan trade, Kai gets to aim them straight at Team Pillbert next week.
bios.6: Kaushal finally won one, posting the week's top score of 140.1 behind CeeDee Lamb's 32.8. His points for rank fourth in the league despite a 1-3 record, so the two-time champ's luck may finally be turning.
bios.7: Ramon still owns the league's best offense by a mile at 561 points for, but Brucie's perfect start ended against the villain he hates most. Title odds slipped from 54 to 43 percent, and a 3-1 showdown with Randy is next.
bios.8: Zoe's rookie season just got real: a 120.88-point upset of the defending champ powered by McMillan's league-best 38.2. At 2-2 with 17 percent playoff odds, Zilgit is suddenly the most dangerous team in the middle of the pack.
